Version packages: 0.2.4 (#147)

This PR was opened by the [Changesets
release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When
you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will
be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release
yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will
be updated.


# Releases
## openfilm@0.2.4

### Patch Changes

- [#148](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/148)
[`0a90640`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/0a90640fa5412ab5501daeeb8f01e83691b9de76)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - The app's own agent
(your own key) keeps a long conversation going when it looks at many
frames. Pictures keep their full quality. A request carries the pictures
of the agent's latest five reads, and at most 32 MB of them; an older
one is left out of the request with a line naming its file, so the agent
can read it again (the conversation keeps them). A model service that
refuses a request as too large (HTTP 413, a proxy's page included) is
tried again at once with half of the older pictures left out, and says
so in the chat; before, every message after it failed the same way.
Settings › Agents says that the agent's rules are the project's own
AGENTS.md.

- [#146](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/pull/146)
[`29346ca`](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/commit/29346ca43b426a014faebafcebe3e8ce3a738faa)
Thanks [@PazChen](https://github.com/PazChen)! - Sound played faster or
slower is heard the moment the speed changes, and sounds natural. The
browser plays it at that speed with its pitch kept, in the same mix,
kept in step with the picture; nothing is made on the server first.
0.2.3 re-encoded the whole sound for each speed, which left long videos
silent for seconds after a change and made voices sound hollow.

The viewer's playback button shows a speed gauge instead of the
inspector's icon.

Studio: the second click of a double-click on a card opens nothing (#151)

## What and why

Cards in the Projects window open on a single click. Many people
double-click out of habit, and on a folder that goes wrong: the first
click opens the folder, its contents take the cards' places, and the
second click lands on whatever project is now under the pointer and
opens it. Double-click a folder and you end up inside one of its
projects.

A card's open now ignores a click whose `detail` is 2 or more
(`opensOnClick` in `lib/projects-page.ts`). Single click still opens.
Enter and Space (`detail` 0) and the card's "…" › Open (no event) work
as before. This applies to project and folder cards, in both the grid
and the list view. Select mode is unchanged.

## Tests

- `lib/projects-page.test.ts`: `opensOnClick` for `detail` 0, 1, 2 and
3.
- Tried on `pnpm dev` in a headless browser, with its own library: a
folder with projects in it, first after "New project".
`page.mouse.dblclick` on the folder card: on `main` a project in the
folder opened; with this change the folder is open and no project is.
- `pnpm --filter openfilm typecheck` and `pnpm audit:public` pass. In
`pnpm --filter openfilm test` every `studio/ui` test passes; on this
Windows PC 13 tests in `src/` and `studio/server/` fail, in files this
PR leaves untouched. CI runs all three systems.

## Checklist

- [x] One change
- [x] A test, if it fixes a bug
- [ ] SPEC.md updated, if it changes film.html (does not)
- [ ] A new media provider (not one)
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` passes; `pnpm test`: see Tests

Co-authored-by: WEBGRS <webgrs@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Studio: keep selection toolbars behind the export dialog (#160)

## What and why

With a timeline selection and a marked range, opening Export leaves the
selection action bar above the export window. Both are portaled to
`body`, but the bar's layer was higher than the export dialog's,
allowing clip actions through the modal.

Keep selection action bars above the workspace and below menus and
dialogs, matching the component's existing intent. The workspace is in a
z10 stacking context and the desktop chat column is z40; global menus
start at z110 and Export is z130. A z100 bar remains above ordinary
editing content while yielding to those overlays. This also puts the bar
below other menus/popovers that previously used smaller layer numbers.

The marked range remains available after closing Export, and Export's
own body-portaled dropdowns remain usable.

## Validation

Windows, Node 24.19.0:

- Real Studio browser regression: failed on unmodified main because the
pointer hit the selection bar above Export; passes with the fix. Checks
both browser hit-testing and a real mouse click, opens and selects a
frame-rate dropdown option, then closes Export and checks that the range
toolbar is reachable again.
- User manual check: confirmed that the reported
selection-toolbar/dialog layering is now correct. This confirmation is
limited to that layering issue; it does not establish manual coverage of
every menu or the independent subtitle fix.
- Existing selection-toolbar placement tests: 10 passed.
- Additional real browser impact checks: 8 passed, covering the timeline
tooltip/context menu and Copy attributes action; clearing a range; stage
clip and HTML text-layer menus; Export and its dropdown; Settings;
playback speed selection; and a 900x650 window. Both fixture films
remained byte-for-byte unchanged and no page errors occurred. The
tracked regression also checks normal timeline and stage toolbar menus.
- Studio UI production build, all workspace typechecks, public audit
including gitleaks, package contents check, and git diff --check passed.
- The actual Electron chat panel was reviewed in source, not exercised
in this browser run.
- The broader test run for the other independent fix found 14
pre-existing failures, all reproduced on unmodified main 53156ac. That
full suite was not repeated for this two-line layer change;
cross-platform CI is pending.

Includes an openfilm patch changeset. No new dependencies or public
configuration.

## Checklist

- [x] One change
- [x] A test, if it fixes a bug
- [x] SPEC.md updated, if it changes film.html — N/A, the format is
unchanged
- [x] A new media provider: tests against a fake service, what the real
service did (never a key), its mark, its words in five languages — N/A
- [ ] `pnpm test` and `pnpm typecheck` pass — typechecks and focused
regressions pass; the full local suite has baseline failures noted above
and cross-platform CI is pending
- [x] Patch changeset for the user-visible fix

commit.message:
Studio: New project inside a folder, made in that folder (#150)

## What and why

Inside a folder of the Projects window there was no "New project":
`showNew` was `folderId === null && !query.trim()`, so the cell only
showed at the top level. To start a film in a folder you had to make it
at the top level and move it with "Move to…".

Now "New project" starts the list in a folder too, and the project it
makes is filed in that folder (`PUT /api/projects/:id/folder`) before it
opens. If filing fails (the folder was deleted in the meantime), the
project still opens and sits at the top level. The examples still show
at the top level only.

`projects.folderEmpty` ("This folder is empty") is gone from the five
languages: a folder now always shows "New project", so the string had no
place left.

## Tests

- `lib/project-folders.test.ts`: `listStarts` (New project at the top
level and in a folder, not over search results; examples at the top
level only) and `newProjectIn` (files the project before it opens, does
not file at the top level, keeps the project when filing fails, throws
when the project can't be made).
- Tried on `pnpm dev` in a headless browser, with its own
`OPENFILM_LIBRARY` and `OPENFILM_SHARED_HOME`: made a folder, opened it,
pressed New project. The new project opened and `/api/projects` listed
it with that folder's `folderId`. The same script on `main` finds no New
project button in the folder.
- `pnpm --filter openfilm typecheck` and `pnpm audit:public` pass. In
`pnpm --filter openfilm test` every `studio/ui` test passes; on this
Windows PC 13 tests in `src/` and `studio/server/` fail, in files this
PR leaves untouched. CI runs all three systems.

## Checklist

- [x] One change
- [x] A test, if it fixes a bug
- [ ] SPEC.md updated, if it changes film.html (does not)
- [ ] A new media provider (not one)
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` passes; `pnpm test`: see Tests

showed at the top level. To start a film in a folder you had to make it
at the top level and move it with "Move to…".

Now "New project" starts the list in a folder too, and the project it
makes is filed in that folder (`PUT /api/projects/:id/folder`) before it
opens. If filing fails (the folder was deleted in the meantime), the
project still opens and sits at the top level. The examples still show
at the top level only.

`projects.folderEmpty` ("This folder is empty") is gone from the five
languages: a folder now always shows "New project", so the string had no
place left.

## Tests

- `lib/project-folders.test.ts`: `listStarts` (New project at the top
level and in a folder, not over search results; examples at the top
level only) and `newProjectIn` (files the project before it opens, does
not file at the top level, keeps the project when filing fails, throws
when the project can't be made).
- Tried on `pnpm dev` in a headless browser, with its own
`OPENFILM_LIBRARY` and `OPENFILM_SHARED_HOME`: made a folder, opened it,
pressed New project. The new project opened and `/api/projects` listed
it with that folder's `folderId`. The same script on `main` finds no New
project button in the folder.
- `pnpm --filter openfilm typecheck` and `pnpm audit:public` pass. In
`pnpm --filter openfilm test` every `studio/ui` test passes; on this
Windows PC 13 tests in `src/` and `studio/server/` fail, in files this
PR leaves untouched. CI runs all three systems.

- [x] One change
- [x] A test, if it fixes a bug
- [ ] SPEC.md updated, if it changes film.html (does not)
- [ ] A new media provider (not one)
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` passes; `pnpm test`: see Tests
